label: Cisco 2811 integrated services router
description: The branch router every Packet Tracer lab starts with: two onboard 10/100 FastEthernet ports, an HWIC/WIC slot pair for WAN interfaces, and a console port. Modelled here with a WIC-2T in the first HWIC slot, which is what gives it the two synchronous serial ports this engine used to have no concept of.
notes: Cisco 2811: two integrated 10/100 FastEthernet ports, four HWIC slots (two of them double-wide), one network-module slot, one AIM slot, console and auxiliary ports. The serial ports are not onboard: they come from a WIC-2T in an HWIC slot, and the two modelled here (Se0/0/0, Se0/0/1) are that card in the first slot. Each serial port is a V.35 socket; a lab cables two of these back to back, and exactly one end of the cable supplies the clock ('clock rate'), which the link validator enforces - two DCE ends or none is refused, because a synchronous serial line nobody clocks carries nothing. The 10/100 ports are 100 Mbps, not 1 Gbps: the 2811 predates GigabitEthernet onboard and a lab that expects 1G here is describing a 2911.
